newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa comfortable after breathing problems.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa comfortable after breathing problems.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in intensive care recovering from heart surgery, was comfortable after respiratory therapy to clear congestion in her lungs, doctors said on Friday.
"Mother Teresa is still not out of danger," Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular medical update.

It said the 86-year-old nun still suffered from bronchial pneumonia and her lungs had become more congested overnight. "Continuous respiratory therapy is being given," it said. Mother Teresa has been receiving chest massages to clear up congestion.
Last month, the Roman Catholic missionary had heart surgery to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She had similar surgery in 1991 in the United States and in 1993 at the Birla clinic.

On Wednesday, doctors gave her a mild electric shock to correct an irregular heart beat. Afterwards, they said the procedure, during which Mother Teresa remained conscious but under sedation, was a success.

But her recovery has been complicated by nagging bronchitis. Doctors have said they would like her to be back at her Missionaries of Charity religious order by Christmas, but that there is no assurance.
"Cardiovascular status is stabilising. Her rhythm is still regular and her pumping force showed some improvement," the medical update said.
The clinic said the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner had her morning tea. "She walked a little and attended Mass sitting on a chair," it said.
The revered missionary has been pressing doctors to let her return to her religious order to resume her work with the sick and dying, for which she has been dubbed "Saint of the Gutters".
But doctors have cautioned that her recovery will be slow and she might never be as active as before.
